classification.difficultyReason: Construct the two radii to expose triangles sharing OM, combine equal radii and midpoint lengths for SSS, then connect equal matching angles with their straight-line sum to prove perpendicularity. The construction and final connection are unscaffolded, although the congruence method is familiar.

content.prompt: $AB$ is a chord of a circle centre $O$ and $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$. Prove that $OM$ is perpendicular to $AB$.

answer.short:
$OM\perp AB$.

By SSS, $\triangle OAM\equiv\triangle OBM$. The matching angles at $M$ are equal and supplementary, so each is $90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Join $OA$ and $OB$. In triangles $OAM$ and $OBM$:
$$\begin{align*}OA&=OB&&\text{(radii)}\\AM&=BM&&\text{(}M\text{ is the midpoint of }AB\text{)}\\OM&=OM&&\text{(common side)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle OAM\equiv\triangle OBM$ (SSS), so $\angle OMA=\angle OMB$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).

Since $A$, $M$ and $B$ lie on a straight line,
$$\begin{align*}\angle OMA+\angle OMB&=180^\circ\\2\angle OMA&=180^\circ\\\angle OMA&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Hence $OM\perp AB$.
